name: Facial Muscle Physics
description: Analyzes facial muscle movement physics to detect synthetic artifacts, anomalies, and characteristic signatures of generative AI models.
algorithm: Facial Muscle Physics — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method verifies facial muscle physics for deepfake detection:

1. **Muscle Group Activation Mapping**: Key facial muscle groups are tracked via action unit proxy: frontalis (forehead), orbicularis oculi (eyes), zygomaticus major (smile), depressor anguli oris (frown), mentalis (chin). Their activations are mapped per frame based on landmark deformations.

2. **Biomechanical Constraint Verification**: Facial muscles obey physical constraints: (a) muscles can only pull, not push, (b) paired muscles produce predictable opposing forces, (c) muscle force follows the force-velocity relationship. The method checks whether observed landmark deformations are achievable through valid muscle activation patterns.

3. **Tissue Deformation Physics**: When muscles contract, surrounding soft tissue deforms following viscoelastic dynamics — skin stretches with wrinkle formation, subcutaneous tissue displaces causing bulging. The method verifies that tissue deformation patterns are consistent with underlying muscle activation. Deepfakes may produce facial deformations without physically correct tissue response.

4. **Inter-Muscle Coupling**: Anatomically, facial muscles share fascia and tissue connections, creating biomechanical coupling. Contracting the zygomaticus (smile) inevitably affects cheek position and orbicularis oculi. The method checks whether these biomechanical couplings are preserved. AI generators often move facial features independently, ignoring muscle coupling.

5. **Dynamic Response Properties**: Muscles exhibit specific dynamic properties: inertia (can't start/stop instantly), elastic recoil, and fatigue. The method analyzes the dynamic response of facial movements — natural movements show smooth acceleration/deceleration following these properties. Deepfake facial dynamics often violate these constraints, producing movements with unnatural jerk profiles.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through facial muscle physics analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
